blocks.content: This closing topic brings together HPA, VPA, and Cluster Autoscaler, three genuinely different levers operating at three different levels, and how they are actually combined, or avoided, in real production practice.

As covered across this module: HPA adjusts how many Pods exist, VPA adjusts how big each individual Pod is, and Cluster Autoscaler adjusts how many nodes the cluster itself has, three genuinely distinct, complementary tools.

blocks.alt: Three distinct tools, working at three genuinely different levels of the stack

blocks.content: This module's entire subject is the automatic counterpart to the manual kubectl scale covered in the Deployments module, both change the same underlying replica count, the difference is purely whether a human or a metric is making the decision.

blocks.alt: The same underlying lever, decided by a human or decided automatically by a metric

blocks.content: In practice, HPA and Cluster Autoscaler paired together is the most common real production setup, HPA reacts quickly to changing Pod-level demand, and Cluster Autoscaler ensures the underlying node capacity keeps up, adding machines when HPA's new Pods genuinely have nowhere to run.

blocks.alt: The pairing that actually shows up most often in real, working production clusters

blocks.content: Worth restating directly from the VPA topic, running VPA and HPA together on the exact same metric creates real, unresolved conflict, a combination generally avoided rather than actively pursued in practice.

blocks.alt: A combination to actively avoid, not one to casually reach for

blocks.content: The right combination genuinely depends on the workload, a stateless web service with variable traffic fits HPA plus Cluster Autoscaler naturally, a workload with genuinely unpredictable, hard-to-right-size resource needs per replica might reach for VPA alone, instead of alongside HPA.

blocks.alt: A deliberate choice, matched to the actual workload, not a one-size-fits-all default

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: HPA, VPA, and Cluster Autoscaler work at three different levels, Pod count, Pod size, and node count, and are chosen deliberately based on what a workload actually needs.
HPA plus Cluster Autoscaler is the most common real production pairing, VPA alongside HPA on the same metric is a real conflict, generally avoided rather than combined.
